title: Inference for cumulative intraday return curves

original_source.central_claim: The functional two-sample beta test has correct asymptotic size and useful power under its dependence assumptions and reveals financial-crisis/oil effects missed by point returns.; FPCA scores combined with peaks-over-threshold analysis quantify extreme CIDR magnitude and shape and reveal sector-specific crisis risk changes.; The mixed-model/bootstrap multiple-testing extension does not control FDR for the motivating very small biological samples.

central_claims: The functional two-sample beta test has correct asymptotic size and useful power under its dependence assumptions and reveals financial-crisis/oil effects missed by point returns.
FPCA scores combined with peaks-over-threshold analysis quantify extreme CIDR magnitude and shape and reveal sector-specific crisis risk changes.
The mixed-model/bootstrap multiple-testing extension does not control FDR for the motivating very small biological samples.

source_manifest.title: Inference for cumulative intraday return curves
source_manifest.finding: Dissertation chapters 2 and 3 reproduce the author’s 2017 beta-test article and 2018-online extreme-risk article; chapter 4 reports a small-sample FDR limitation.

source_manifest.title: Functional Data Analysis in Econometrics
source_manifest.finding: Frončková and Pražák synthesize 55 econometric applications; section 2 includes the exact chapter articles as stock-index and investment-risk applications.

source_manifest.title: Functional Spherical Autocorrelation: A Robust Estimate of the Autocorrelation of a Functional Time Series
source_manifest.finding: Yeh, Rice and Dubin cite the extreme-risk chapter article when describing CIDR data; their autocorrelation construction does not reuse its FPCA/EVT risk procedure.

source_manifest.title: Forecasting intraday financial time series with sieve bootstrapping and dynamic updating
source_manifest.finding: Shang and Ji implement other forecasting and bootstrap methods; their Kokoszka 2017 citation is the separate autocovariance paper, not Zheng’s beta-test chapter.

answers.rationale: The synthesis categorizes the financial chapters; the primary follow-ups examine other CIDR methods. None explicitly verifies the beta-test properties, sector-risk conclusions or biological FDR result.
No independent rerun of the beta test, extreme-region estimator or biological simulation was located.
Later financial datasets were analyzed with different methods, leaving stricter tests of the dissertation methods unverified.
The synthesis recognizes applications but does not explicitly assess the three recorded central claims.
No follow-up tested the stationarity/independent-period assumptions, extreme-angle estimation limitations or small-sample FDR failure.
Spherical autocorrelation and sieve forecasting are different constructions; a substantive extension of the beta test or risk estimator was not established.
Independent authors cite relevant chapter publications, but two teams substantively building on those specific constructions were not demonstrated.
The later primary studies use CIDR representations originating before this dissertation, not its particular beta test or extreme-risk procedure.
The review describes existing application areas without crediting these chapters as enabling a new direction.
No later benchmark directly comparing the dissertation beta test or extreme-risk estimator was read.
Later forecasting benefits concern other methods; no independent practical benefit attributable to these specific constructions was verified.
Applications to other assets do not establish successful transfer of the dissertation methods when only the older CIDR representation is shared.
The later spherical-correlation and sieve-bootstrap results were not shown to require the dissertation’s specific contributions.
No documented trading or risk-management workflow using the proposed beta test or extreme-region procedure was found.
No independent fair comparison tested the claimed additional information relative to point-to-point returns for these methods.
The 2022/2023 papers do not establish substantive reuse of the specific methods; the 2021 review’s exact timing relative to the fall-2018 dissertation is uncertain.
The application synthesis is dated 2021 but a full three-year interval from the dissertation is not established; later background citations are insufficient.
One independent synthesis was verified; primary citations in other years did not establish substantive follow-up of the specific contribution.

An independent literature synthesis includes both published financial chapters as examples of applicable functional econometrics. This supports synthesis uptake only, not replication of the dissertation’s central claims.

evidence.explanation: Section 2 and its references identify the exact beta-test and extreme-risk chapter publications.

answers.rationale: No later comparison explicitly concludes these methods remain useful despite newer alternatives.

search_gaps: The complete dissertation was available; selected main-text methods, results and conclusions were read, not every proof or numerical table.
Two chapters were published separately in 2017 and 2018-online/2019-print; later chapter citations are mapped explicitly rather than treated as new studies.
Some publisher full-text leads were inaccessible; no follow-up to the biological multiple-testing chapter was verified.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; the assigned pilot sample is not an unbiased estimate of all research outcomes.
research.summary: An independent synthesis recognizes the financial chapters as applications. Specific independent validation and operational use remain unresolved; generic CIDR research is not credited to this dissertation.
